chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said:

A man said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I am weak in deeds and few in fasting, but I hope that I do not eat except what is permissible.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Which striving is superior to chastity of the belly and the private part?'
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior form of striving according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the practical discipline of consuming only halal sustenance and guarding one's chastity above the quantity of ritual worship, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the purity of the self as a foundation for spiritual validity. This teaching underscores that 'chastity of the belly' (referring to lawful income and consumption) is a profound form of ijtihad, ensuring that one's body, the vessel for worship, remains pure and acceptable to God. It reflects the broader scholarly view that neglecting halal sustenance can invalidate even abundant acts of devotion.
